subject: HelioEdge: Post-upgrade latency + error spike — potential contract/SLA risk
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@helioedge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Gomez <natalie@helioedge.com>
Date: 2026-08-01 09:12 -0700
Subject: Prod degradation after v4.2 rollout — urgent

Irene —

We pushed the 4.2 model image yesterday based on your team's guidance (quant profile qv2). Since 02:00 UTC we're seeing: p95 latency up from 320ms -> 1.1s, error rate (5xx) creeping to ~3.4%, and token throughput down ~28%. This is impacting checkout flows and we're getting alerts from our ops team.

Attached is a snapshot from our observability stack covering 01:30–09:00 UTC (helioedge_slo_incident_snapshot_20260801.zip).

This is an enterprise account and the SLA/uptime clause is explicit — we need immediate remediation and visibility into an action plan and timeline. Please advise how quickly Redwood can:

- revert to previous model variant or qprofile
- provide expected rollback duration and risk
- propose short-term mitigations to reduce latency and errors

I'm copying our procurement lead Natalie since if this degrades beyond threshold we will discuss credits and an exec call.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Head of Platform — HelioEdge


From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@helioedge.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Natalie Gomez <natalie@helioedge.com>
Date: 2026-08-01 09:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod degradation after v4.2 rollout — urgent

Tom —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachment. We see the same signal on our side (ingested your snapshot). Immediate next steps from Redwood:

1) Triage & short-term rollback: Marissa (serving/runtime) is on call and recommends a canary revert to v4.1 + qv1 for the hotpath. This should reduce p95 substantially and stop the error spikes.
2) Data & logs: please share a subset of affected request ids — 5–10 example request_ids and a sample user payload so we can reproduce the error.
3) Communication cadence: we'll open an incident channel (INC-20260801-HE) and provide 30-min updates until resolved.

Marissa — can you confirm whether a canary revert can be done with zero config changes on HelioEdge's side and an ETA for rollback?

Stephanie — can you own the customer comms and credit/contract triage if this hits SLA?

Tom/Natalie — we will not perform any irreversible actions without your explicit signoff; we want permission to run the canary revert.

Irene
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom@helioedge.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01 10:08 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod degradation after v4.2 rollout — urgent

Folks — quick technical triage below. I pulled traces and KV cache telemetry from HelioEdge's serving lane. Initial findings:

- The qv2 quant profile reduces model size but increases dequant ops on the hot path; we see increased GPU kernel latency for long-context calls (>1024 tokens).
- Concurrently, we noticed an edge case in the continuous-batching heuristic where prefix cache eviction frequency increased, which magnifies tail latency under customer workload.
- Error rate (5xx) appears correlated with OOM-retries on one secondary shard during high concurrency windows; logs attached in the incident link.

Plan (short):
- With HelioEdge signoff we can initiate a canary revert of 20% traffic back to v4.1/qv1 within 15 minutes; monitor for 30 minutes; if stable, promote full revert (target 60–90 minutes end-to-end).
- If revert is not acceptable, we can instead patch the batching heuristic (hotfix) — ~2–3 hours to rollout and validate in prod.

I'm attaching the rollback MOP (redwood_mop_rollback_v1.docx) and a quick checklist. Risks: the canary revert is low-risk but will briefly double write amplification on cache; the hotfix is medium-risk but avoids model change.

Requesting explicit authorization: "approve_canary_revert" from HelioEdge (Tom or Natalie). If approved we will proceed and update this thread + incident channel.

—Marissa
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reynolds <tom@helioedge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Gomez <natalie@helioedge.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01 10:25 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod degradation after v4.2 rollout — urgent

Marissa/Irene —

Approve canary revert now. Please move 20% to v4.1/qv1 and report p95 and 5xx every 15 mins. We need the shortest path to stabilize checkout.

Also: per our contract, if this incident exceeds the 30-minute p95 SLA window we will expect remediation credits. Natalie (copied) will coordinate. Please send a post-incident summary so we can follow procurement steps.

Tom

On a related note — is there a plan to avoid this qprofile/heuristic interaction going forward? We want a mitigation so we can continue to adopt smaller quant profiles without risking production regressions.

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom@helioedge.com>, Natalie Gomez <natalie@helioedge.com>
Date: 2026-08-03 16:45 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary & decision request — HelioEdge incident (post-mitigation)

Team —

Summary (post-mitigation):
- Timeline: 2026-08-01 09:12 UTC alert → canary revert approved by HelioEdge at 10:25 → 20% traffic reverted by 10:40 → full revert completed by 11:05.
- Impact: p95 reduced from ~1.1s to ~340ms within the canary window; 5xx dropped from 3.4% to 0.2%. Throughput returned to baseline.
- Root cause (high-level): interaction between qv2's dequant hotpath and our continuous-batching prefix eviction heuristic under HelioEdge's long-context workload. One secondary shard experienced OOM retries which elevated 5xx.

Asks / decisions for leadership:
1) Customer remediation credits — Stephanie, please estimate exposure. HelioEdge is asking for SLA credits per contract DL-94827.
2) Product fix prioritization — Marissa requests 5 engineer-days to implement a heuristic guardrail + a qprofile compatibility test in our CI (pre-deploy sim with representative long-context traces). Approve for P1 in next sprint?
3) Communication — we should send HelioEdge a formal RCA doc and a targeted mitigation roadmap. Tom expects this before the procurement meeting next week.

Attachments included in internal ticket: qprofile-performance-summary.csv and the rollback MOP used. I recommend we approve the 5 engineer-days and prepare the RCA; this minimizes executive exposure and reduces the chance of repeat regression.

Irene
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
